If no right of return exists, the seller has to say so in writing. Used, recased or reconditioned instruments must be marked. Read that page before you sign, because in Missouri the agreement is the protection.

One more Missouri rule worth knowing for families: for a purchaser under eighteen, state law requires an examination by an otolaryngologist, a Missouri-licensed physician, or a licensed audiologist, with a written recommendation issued within ninety days before the fitting.

### What does this look like from behind the counter?

Hearing practices don’t make money the way customers picture. Under the bundled model the FDA described in its 2022 rule, years of service are priced into one transaction — the fitting, the reprogram at week six, the remake when a dome won’t seat, the tubing change three winters later. All of it was paid for on day one and never again. Meanwhile Medicare reimburses nothing for the fitting exam, so the single appointment that most determines whether a patient succeeds is the one no insurer pays for. The calendar is lumpy too: with Medicare open enrollment ending December 7 and new plan benefits starting January 1, a quiet autumn turns into a January of people arriving with a freshly reset allowance. Owners talk to each other about the returns and about patients who never wore the aids long enough to adapt. Being findable when a neighbor finally searches is the other half of it, which is where a complete directory listing earns its keep.

Ready to stop guessing at the dinner table? Browse hearing aid providers across the St. Louis metro on St Louis Near Me Directory, then call two of them and ask the same five questions from the top of this page. Hospital billing has its own rules worth knowing before any procedure: charity care and the billing rights nobody mentions.

### Frequently asked questions

### Q. What is the Trump hearing aid act?

A.  That phrase refers to the Over-the-Counter Hearing Aid Act of 2017, introduced in the Senate as S.670 and folded into the FDA Reauthorization Act of 2017, signed August 18, 2017. It directed the FDA to create a category of hearing aids adults could buy without a prescription. The agency finalized those regulations in August 2022, and the OTC category took effect October 17, 2022.

### Q. What is the best hearing aid available right now?

A.  No honest answer names a model. Hearing aids are matched to a specific pattern of loss, a specific ear canal, and a specific set of listening situations, so a device that changes one person’s life underperforms for the next. Round-up articles rank features and prices, which is real information, but they haven’t tested your ears. Only a clinician who measures your hearing can say what fits your loss.

### Q. What hearing aid do most audiologists recommend?

A.  There is no consensus brand. A clinic’s shelf is shaped by manufacturer relationships, buying groups, insurance contracts, and which fitting software the staff knows cold — worth knowing rather than resenting. Ask directly: which manufacturers do you fit, and why that one for my results? A provider who answers specifically about your audiogram tells you more than any brand name would.

### Q. What is the number one rated hearing aid?

A.  Ratings come from reviewers comparing features, app quality, battery life and price, and they change every year. None of them ranks the thing that decides your outcome: how accurately the device is programmed to your ears, and how consistently you wear it. Treat a top rating as a shortlist, not a prescription, and get the trial terms in writing before money changes hands.

### Q. What is the average cost of a behind-the-ear hearing aid?

A.  No official average exists by style, and style is a weak predictor of price. Behind-the-ear housings span the whole range, from basic to premium, because the cost tracks the technology tier and the services bundled with it. The National Council on Aging cites roughly $2,500 to $3,690 for a pair of prescription aids nationally, with OTC options starting near $200. Ask for an itemized quote instead of a style-based estimate.

### Q. Do I need a doctor’s order to see an audiologist?

A.  Not necessarily. Medicare beneficiaries can see an audiologist once every 12 months without an order for non-acute hearing conditions, though that exception does not extend to hearing aid fitting exams. Private plans set their own referral rules, so call the number on your card first. If you have ear pain, drainage, sudden change, or loss in only one ear, start with a physician instead.

### Q. Can I buy hearing aids online in Missouri?

A.  Yes for OTC devices, if you’re 18 or older and believe your loss is mild to moderate. The FDA allows purchase in a store or online with no exam or prescription. Prescription devices still run through a licensed professional. Before ordering, read the manufacturer’s return policy printed on the outside of the box, since FDA rules require it to appear there and do not require any warranty.

## When You Actually Need a Family Law Attorney in St. Louis
Source: https://stlouismissourinearme.com/blog/when-you-need-a-family-law-attorney-st-louis

Imagine it’s a Wednesday night in Affton and you’re sitting in your own driveway with the engine off, because walking through the door means the same conversation you have already had four times this month. Nobody threw anything. Nobody is a villain. You just know, in the flat way people know these things, that it is over.

Or maybe it isn’t a marriage at all. Maybe you’re a dad in Florissant whose name is on the birth certificate, who just learned that is not the same thing as a custody order. Maybe you’re in Belleville and a parenting schedule from three years ago stopped matching anybody’s real life. Maybe you’re in Kirkwood and your ex quit a job the week after the support order landed.

Those are four different problems, and only some of them need a lawyer. One thing first: this article is general information about how family law works in Missouri and Illinois. It is not legal advice, it is not about your case, and nothing here predicts what a judge will do with your facts. What it can do is hand you the vocabulary before a consultation, so the hour you pay for goes to your situation instead of definitions.

### When do you actually need a family law attorney?

You need one when the other side disputes something, when a court order has to be created or changed, or when the money is complicated. No children, no house, no retirement accounts, both of you agreeing on paper — that is the narrow case people handle themselves. The facts that reliably mean hire someone: children whose schedule you two do not agree on; a business, a pension or a 401(k) to divide; a self-employed spouse who controls the books; any allegation of abuse; an order somebody is ignoring; or a case where the other side already has counsel and you don’t.

Missouri builds in one deadline that catches people flat. Under RSMo 452.310, in any proceeding involving custody or visitation, the petitioner and respondent each have to submit a proposed parenting plan — individually or jointly — within thirty days after service of process or the filing of an entry of appearance, whichever comes first. That is not much time to design the next several years of a child’s life, and the clock runs whether or not you have found help.

Where abuse or neglect is alleged, Missouri removes the discretion: RSMo 452.423 says the court shall appoint a guardian ad litem in any proceeding in which child abuse or neglect is alleged. In other contested custody or support matters that appointment is optional. Either way the guardian ad litem is a third attorney in the room representing the child, and the court can order the parties to pay those fees.

### Is Missouri a 50/50 state for divorce?

No. Missouri divides marital property equitably, not equally. RSMo 452.330 directs the court to divide the marital property and marital debts “in such proportions as the court deems just” after considering the listed factors — and just is not a synonym for half.

The statute names the factors: the economic circumstances of each spouse when the division takes effect, including whether the family home should go to the parent who has custody; each spouse’s contribution to acquiring the marital property, expressly including the contribution of a spouse as homemaker; the value of non-marital property set apart to each spouse; the conduct of the parties during the marriage; and custodial arrangements for the minor children. No formula, no fixed weighting. The trial judge weighs them.

What even counts as marital is its own argument. RSMo 452.330 defines marital property as everything acquired after the marriage except property acquired by gift, bequest, devise or descent, property acquired in exchange for property owned before the marriage, property excluded by a valid written agreement, and the increase in value of premarital property. The house you owned in Maryland Heights before the wedding starts outside the pot; mixing it with marital money is how it gets pulled in. There is one place 50/50 has real footing here, and it is not the bank accounts.

### What rights do fathers have in Missouri?

The same rights mothers have, in writing. RSMo 452.375.8 says that as between the parents of a child, no preference may be given to either parent in the awarding of custody because of that parent’s age, sex, or financial status, nor because of the age or sex of the child. That language has been in the statute for decades.

What moved recently is the starting point on parenting time. Senate Bill 35 took effect August 28, 2023, and put into RSMo 452.375.2 a rebuttable presumption that an award of equal or approximately equal parenting time to each parent is in the best interests of the child. Rebuttable matters — it is a default evidence can overcome, not a guarantee. But the default moved, and it surprises fathers who assumed every other weekend was the ceiling.

For unmarried fathers the real gap is paternity, not parenting. Signing a birth certificate is not a custody order. Under RSMo 210.823 a signed acknowledgment of paternity is treated as a legal finding of paternity, and either party may rescind it by filing with the bureau within sixty days of the last signature; after that, undoing it takes fraud, duress or a material mistake of fact. Legal fatherhood and an enforceable schedule are two separate pieces of paper, and you can hold the first while owning nothing a school will act on.

### How long does a Missouri divorce take?

Missouri sets a floor, not an average. Under RSMo 452.305 the court may enter a judgment of dissolution only if one of you has been a resident of the state for the ninety days immediately preceding the commencement of the proceeding, thirty days have elapsed since the filing of the petition, and the court finds there remains no reasonable likelihood that the marriage can be preserved — that it is irretrievably broken.

Thirty days is the earliest a genuinely agreed case can close. Contested cases run on discovery, appraisals, evaluations and the circuit’s docket, and a year is ordinary. Child support carries its own machinery: Missouri Supreme Court Rule 88.01 presumes a correctly calculated Form 14 amount is the correct amount, and a court departing from it must find, in writing or on the record, that the Form 14 figure is unjust or inappropriate.

Unrelated, and we know it — a dead outlet needs a licensed electrician.

### What is different on the Illinois side?

Illinois runs on a different statute, and this metro straddles the line. Illinois also requires ninety days of residence before a judgment under 750 ILCS 5/401, and it also runs on irreconcilable differences causing an irretrievable breakdown. Parenting is where the two states part company.

Illinois stopped using the word custody in 2016. What Missouri calls legal and physical custody, Illinois splits into significant decision-making responsibility and parenting time, under 750 ILCS 5/602.5 and 5/602.7. And Illinois has no equal-time presumption. Section 602.7 presumes both parents are fit and bars restricting parenting time unless the court finds by a preponderance of the evidence that a parent’s exercise of it would seriously endanger the child’s physical, mental, moral, or emotional health. Allocation itself turns on best interests, with no thumb on the scale toward an even split.

Spousal support diverges the same way. Under 750 ILCS 5/504(b-1), where the parties’ combined gross annual income is under $500,000 and the payor has no prior support obligation, Illinois guideline maintenance is 33 1/3 percent of the payor’s net annual income minus 25 percent of the payee’s net, capped so the payee keeps no more than 40 percent of combined net income. Missouri publishes nothing of the kind — RSMo 452.335 is a list of factors a judge weighs case by case. If one of you lives in Belleville and the other in Kirkwood, where the case lands is not a small detail.

### How much does a divorce attorney cost in Missouri?

There is no honest single number, and any figure pinned to a named firm would be stale within weeks. Four variables do almost all of the work.

Contested versus uncontested. The biggest factor by a wide margin. An agreed case with a signed settlement is essentially a drafting job; a contested case is discovery, depositions, motions and hearings, every hour billed.

Retainer versus hourly. The retainer is usually an advance deposit held in a client trust account and billed against in tenths of an hour, with a clause requiring you to top it up. It is not the price of the divorce. It is the opening balance.

Whether children are involved. A disputed parenting plan, a guardian ad litem, a custody evaluation, a later modification — each adds hours, plus outside fees separate from your attorney’s bill.

How complicated the money is. A closely held business, a pension needing a qualified domestic relations order, self-employment income, or a spouse who controls the records. Each adds an expert, and experts bill too.

Worth raising in the first call: Missouri allows limited scope representation. Rule 4-1.2(c) lets a lawyer limit the work with the client’s written, signed consent setting out the essential terms and the lawyer’s limited role, and Rule 43.01(b), effective July 1, 2010, recognizes an entry of limited appearance. So you may be able to hire someone to draft the parenting plan or appear at one hearing without buying the whole case. Not every firm offers it. Asking is free.

### How do I find a good family law lawyer?

Start with fit, not badges. You want someone who practices family law regularly in the county where the case will actually sit — St. Louis County, St. Charles, Jefferson, Franklin, St. Clair, Madison — because the local judge, the local guardians ad litem and the local docket habits are half the job.

Verify the license first. The Missouri Bar publishes an official directory of Missouri lawyers in good standing with the Supreme Court of Missouri, updated daily and free to search. Illinois attorneys register with the Attorney Registration and Disciplinary Commission of the Supreme Court of Illinois, which runs its own free public lookup. Two minutes, both sides of the river.

Then use the consultation properly. Bring three years of tax returns, recent pay stubs, a list of accounts and debts, and any existing order. Ask how many cases like yours this attorney handled last year, who will work the file day to day, how fast calls get returned, and what the written fee agreement says before you sign. Anyone who guarantees an outcome twenty minutes after hearing your facts is telling you something. If a company the two of you built is tangled in the split, that is a different bench — our guide to when a St. Louis business needs an attorney covers that side.

### What does this look like from the other side of the desk?

Family law bills in tenths of an hour against an advance held in a client trust account — and the household that funded that advance is becoming two households. The final invoice lands when money is tightest, and withdrawing after counsel has entered takes leave of court. That arithmetic sits behind every fee agreement in this metro.

The calendar is lopsided too. Julie Brines and Brian Serafini of the University of Washington, studying filings from 2001 to 2015, found divorce filings peaked in March and August, right after the winter and summer holidays; the pattern repeated in Ohio, Minnesota, Florida and Arizona. December is quiet. The people who file in March mostly decided in December.

What separates the strong operators is what they do with the hours that do not need a lawyer: routing the venting to a paralegal, flat-quoting genuinely uncontested work, offering limited scope help instead of turning someone away. Nobody browses for this the way they browse for dinner — they search the night it lands. Firms can add or claim a listing so that search finds them.

### What if you cannot afford a lawyer at all?

Free civil legal help exists on both sides of the river, income-qualified rather than first-come. Legal Services of Eastern Missouri serves low-income Missourians across 21 eastern Missouri counties, St. Louis City, St. Louis County, St. Charles, Jefferson and Franklin among them. Its general intake does not take routine family law, but its Lasting Solutions program handles family law matters for survivors of domestic violence in St. Louis City, St. Louis County, St. Charles County and Jefferson County. The main line is 314-534-4200.

On the Illinois side, Land of Lincoln Legal Aid serves 65 counties across central and southern Illinois. Its East St. Louis office covers St. Clair, Monroe, Randolph, Clinton and Washington counties; the Alton office covers Madison, Jersey, Macoupin and Bond, among others. Its Legal Advice and Referral Center number is 877-342-7891.

If safety is the immediate problem, that is a faster and separate track from a divorce. Missouri’s Adult Abuse Act, Chapter 455, provides orders of protection, and RSMo 455.025 states that the duties of the clerk prescribed in that section are performed without cost to the litigants. Illinois has a parallel path under its Domestic Violence Act. Neither requires you to have hired an attorney first.

Ready to say it out loud to someone who does this every week? Browse family law attorneys across the St. Louis metro on St Louis Near Me Directory, then shortlist three, check each license, and book the consultations in one week so you can compare the answers while they are fresh. Family budgets get stretched by more than legal fees — how orthodontic costs and insurance actually work is worth reading early.

### Frequently asked questions

### Q. Is a divorce lawyer worth the cost?

A.  It depends on what is in dispute. With no children, no real estate, no retirement accounts and a signed agreement, a lawyer mostly buys correct drafting. Add children, a house, a pension or a spouse who controls the money, and the mistakes an unrepresented party makes tend to cost more than the fee. Some, like a vague parenting plan, follow you for a decade.

### Q. Who is the top-rated family law attorney in St. Louis?

A.  No official ranking exists, and no bar association issues one. The badges you see mix paid directories, peer-nomination lists and review counts, and none of them knows your facts, your county or your budget. A better screen: confirm the license through The Missouri Bar directory or the Illinois ARDC lookup, then judge fit yourself in a consultation.

### Q. What are the three C’s of divorce?

A.  It is a coaching phrase, not a legal standard — usually given as communication, cooperation and compromise. No Missouri or Illinois statute uses it, and no judge applies it. The statutory tests are different animals: Missouri asks whether the marriage is irretrievably broken and divides marital property in the proportions the court deems just, while Illinois runs on irreconcilable differences.

### Q. What is the 80/20 rule for lawyers?

A.  It is the Pareto principle applied to a law practice: roughly 80 percent of results come from roughly 20 percent of inputs, so a small share of clients or tasks drives most of the revenue. That is practice-management shorthand for firm owners, not a rule of law, and it has no bearing on how a judge decides a case.

### Q. Do I still need a lawyer if the divorce is uncontested?

A.  Not necessarily, but uncontested is stricter than most people use it. It means you agree on every item: property, debt, support, and a complete parenting plan you have both signed. If one line is unresolved, it is a contested case with a polite tone. Missouri also permits limited scope representation, so you can pay someone to review the agreement without retaining them for everything.

### Q. Can a Missouri custody order be changed later?

A.  It can be modified, but not because somebody changed their mind. RSMo 452.410 requires facts arising since the prior decree, or unknown to the court then, showing a change in the circumstances of the child or the custodian, plus a finding that modification is necessary to serve the child’s best interests. Informal side agreements are not orders and are not enforceable.

### Q. Does it matter which Missouri county I file in?

A.  Practically, yes. Venue follows residence, and the local circuit sets the rhythm: which judge hears family matters, how parenting plans and Form 14 worksheets are presented, whether mediation gets pushed early, how long the wait for a hearing runs. St. Louis County is a different experience from St. Charles or Jefferson County under identical statutes.

### Q. We live on opposite sides of the river. Which state hears the case?

A.  Worth an early consultation, because Missouri and Illinois answer several of these differently — the parenting-time presumption and spousal maintenance most of all. Both states require ninety days of residence before a dissolution judgment. Which court decides the children’s issues turns on the child’s home state under the interstate custody act both states have adopted.

None of this makes the year easier. It does make the first phone call shorter, and it keeps you from paying by the tenth of an hour to have a parenting plan explained. Write down what you actually want on the other side of this — the schedule, the house, the retirement account, the holidays — before anybody asks you in a conference room.

## Party Equipment Rentals in St. Louis: What to Ask Before You Book
Source: https://stlouismissourinearme.com/blog/what-to-ask-before-booking-party-rentals-st-louis

Imagine it’s the middle of April and the graduation party in Affton just became your problem. The date is fixed. Forty-some people said yes. The backyard is a backyard — a grill, a swing set, a patch of grass that has never held a crowd.

Maybe your version is a fall wedding on a rented lawn in St. Charles, where the ceremony chairs have to be dry at four o’clock. Maybe it’s a church picnic in Florissant, a company family day in Maryland Heights, or a sixtieth birthday in Belleville where half the guests will not stand for three hours. Same phone call.

Here’s the part nobody warns you about. Picking the tent is the easy half. The half that decides how the day runs is a short list of questions asked before any money changes hands.

### What should you ask before you book party equipment rentals?

Six questions, before the deposit. What is the delivery and pickup window? Does the crew set up and tear down, or is this a drop-off? What surface will the tent sit on? What is the weather and cancellation policy, in writing? Who pulls the permit? And what does the damage waiver actually cover?

Those six aren’t arbitrary. They map to the six ways a rental goes sideways. The truck shows up at 7 a.m. Saturday when you wanted Friday. The chairs land stacked on the driveway and setup was extra. The tent can’t be staked because the only flat ground is asphalt. It rains and the deposit is gone. An inspector wants a permit nobody applied for. Get the answers by email.

### What size tent do you need for 100 guests?

For 100 guests seated at round tables, plan on roughly 1,200 square feet of tent — a 30x40 is the bare minimum, and most rental companies will move you up to a 40x60 once you add a buffet line, a bar and any dance floor. A standing cocktail crowd of 100 fits in far less, closer to 600 square feet, because nobody needs a chair or a place to set a plate.

The arithmetic is simple enough to do yourself. Companies size from square feet per person, not headcount: roughly 12 square feet for a guest at a round table, about 8 for ceremony rows, 5 or 6 for standing. Multiply, then add the footprint of anything that isn’t a person.

What size tent do I need for 50 guests? Half the people, roughly half the ground: about 600 square feet seated, which puts a 20x30 at the floor and a 20x40 in comfortable territory. Give them the guest count, the seating style and the extras, then ask them to confirm it fits your yard with room to stake.

### What are the most rented items for parties?

Tables, chairs, linens and tents carry most of the volume in this trade, in that order. They are what nearly every event needs, which is why a rental yard’s chair count is the truest measure of how big it is.

After that come the things that make an event feel finished. Sidewalls and tent lighting for anything running past dusk. Cocktail tables, which quietly reduce how many chairs you need. Chafing dishes, ice tubs, dance floors, portable restrooms for open ground. Heaters in October and fans in July, both of which sell out the same week the weather turns.

Then the family category: inflatables, concession machines, yard games and a sound system somebody’s uncle will take over. If the party is for kids, the bounce house gets booked first — and it carries the most rules.

### Does the price include setup, or is it a drop-off?

Ask directly, because both are common and they price differently. A drop-off means the crew unloads at the curb and leaves; you carry, unfold and stack. Full setup means they place the tables, open the chairs, stake the tent, and return to break it down. Plenty of companies do setup on tents and drop-off on everything else.

Then pin down the window. Most companies deliver on a range, not a time — a four-hour block, sometimes an all-day one. For a Saturday event that often means a Friday delivery and a Monday pickup, and that weekend-long possession is baked into the rate whether you use it or not. Say so up front if your park shelter has to be clear by dark.

### Do you need a permit for a tent in St. Louis?

Inside the City of St. Louis, yes, above a size threshold. The city’s tent and temporary structure policy requires a permit for tents greater than 800 square feet in total area, including multiple tents attached to one another with an aggregate area greater than 800 square feet. Any tent that affects, covers or obstructs a required means of egress needs approval regardless of size. Tents under 800 square feet that block nothing are exempt, as are tents for a private family event on the same residential lot.

Notice where that leaves a 20x40. It is exactly 800 square feet, right on the line, and attaching a 10x10 caterer’s canopy puts the aggregate over. Two other city rules catch people out: fabric has to be flame resistant with a certificate, and tents must be placed on grass so they can be staked — not on pavement. If your only flat ground is a parking lot, the conversation shifts to ballast, and ballast means weight, labor and a different price.

Outside the city limits, the threshold is whatever the local building or fire office says it is — St. Louis County, St. Charles County, Kirkwood and the Illinois municipalities all run their own. Ask the rental company who pulls it. Good operators handle it routinely, but the customer is responsible for all permits is a real sentence in real contracts.

Wildly off-topic — the graduate needs a haircut before the photos.

### Do bounce houses need a permit in Missouri or Illinois?

This is a genuine state-line split, and it matters if your event is in Belleville rather than Ballwin. Illinois regulates inflatables by name: the Illinois Department of Labor’s Amusement Ride and Attraction Safety Division lists inflatable attractions — moonwalks and bounce houses — among equipment that must be inspected before initial operation and annually after, with a permit decal affixed to each unit. Illinois permits run the calendar year.

The rule follows public use, not the equipment. IDOL’s FAQ is explicit that someone who rents an inflatable for a private party does not need a permit; the obligation sits with the owner operating it publicly. IDOL also sets a minimum operator age of 16 and a $1,000,000 per occurrence, $2,000,000 aggregate insurance requirement for permitted operations.

Missouri is different. Its Amusement Ride Safety Act, at RSMo 316.203, defines an amusement ride as mechanical devices that carry passengers, dry slides over 20 feet, trams and motorized wagons, bungee attractions, and climbing walls over 10 feet. Inflatables are not named. So in Illinois, ask to see the current decal. In Missouri there is no state decal — ask instead for the certificate of insurance, the manufacturer’s posted rider limits, and whether an attendant stays.

### What happens if it rains on the day of your event?

Usually the event goes on and the deposit does not come back. Most rental contracts treat a deposit as non-refundable once equipment is loaded, since the item was off the shelf and unavailable to anyone else. That is why the tent is the rain plan rather than a casualty of it.

Three things to settle in writing: how late you can move the date and whether the deposit travels with it, what happens if the crew judges conditions unsafe, and whether sidewalls can be added last minute. Wind is the real decision point, not rain — crews will strike or refuse to raise a tent in gusts, and no reputable operator negotiates that.

If the site is a park, a rented lawn or one of the campgrounds around St. Louis, check its own rules on staking and vehicle access first.

### How can I reduce the cost of party rentals?

Shrink the tent, shrink the chair count, and widen the delivery window — in that order. Those are the three biggest levers, and none of them costs you anything the guests will notice.

It helps to know what drives the number. Tent size and anchoring is the largest single factor: staking into grass is quick, ballasting on pavement adds weights, labor and time. A tight delivery window costs more than a flexible one. Weekend dates carry a premium in peak months because inventory is finite. Damage waivers are usually a percentage add-on, so they scale with everything else on the order.

Practical cuts: move the buffet and the bar outside the tent so you are not renting square footage to shelter a table. Swap a third of the seating for cocktail tables. Use one vendor rather than two delivery fees. And ask what is already going out that weekend — a size sitting idle sometimes prices better.

### How far ahead should you book for graduation and wedding season?

As soon as the date is fixed, and earlier than feels necessary. Late April through early June is graduation season across the metro, and September and October carry the fall weddings. Those weekends are when tent inventory runs out first, and a rental yard cannot conjure a second 40x60 the way a caterer adds a tray.

Chairs and tables usually survive a late request. Tents, dance floors, heaters and specialty linen colors do not. Weekday and Sunday dates hold availability much longer. If the event is a wedding, the rental calendar and the bridal shop timeline in St. Louis run on the same months, and both reward booking early for the same reason: finite stock, fixed dates.

### Are event rentals profitable?

They can be, and the shape of it surprises people. The American Rental Association’s May 8, 2026 forecast, built with S&P Global Market Intelligence, put the U.S. event rental industry on track to grow 8 percent in 2026 to $6.1 billion. But the margin isn’t where customers assume. A big frame tent is capital that pays back across seasons, not on one weekend. Linens carry the best percentage and the worst labor, because somebody launders and folds every one between events. The money is really made or lost on the truck — how many stops a two-person crew clears in a window.

The year is made in two stretches, graduations and fall weddings, and January is quiet enough to hurt. What operators grumble about is short: the Saturday-in-May call placed ten days out, and the tent booked for a driveway that cannot be staked. Since this search starts with a category and a location, a complete, current directory listing is how a yard gets found.

Date set, backyard still empty?
